traps.trap: Trendelenburg operation with stripping is the first-line treatment for SFJ incompetence

probes.stem_idea: Symptomatic GSV reflux confirmed on duplex, patient fit for any procedure: what is the current first-line treatment?
probes.correct: Endothermal ablation (radiofrequency or laser)
probes.note: foam is correct-adjacent (second line); the trap is the memorised PYQ key

probes.stem_idea: Which pairing correctly states what older PYQs expected versus what current practice recommends?
probes.correct: PYQ key: Trendelenburg with stripping; current: endothermal ablation first
distractor_set: PYQ key: endothermal ablation; current: Trendelenburg with stripping first
PYQ key and current practice both name foam sclerotherapy first
PYQ key: stripping alone; current: compression hosiery first

probes.stem_idea: Arrange the current stepwise ladder for truncal reflux: which is offered when the first option is unsuitable?
probes.correct: Foam sclerotherapy, then open surgery only if both unsuitable
distractor_set: Open surgery next, foam only after surgery fails
Compression hosiery next, then open surgery
Open surgery and foam are offered together as equal first choices

traps.diagnoses: Learner has memorised the old PYQ key as the answer and has not updated the treatment order to current practice.
traps.first_wrong_step: Sees 'SFJ incompetence' in the stem and retrieves the classic operation by association, without asking which option the question's 'current' or 'first-line' wording points to.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - 'PYQs expected X; current practice is Y' - and give a rule for which to pick when the stem says current/first-line vs classic

traps.retest: contrast probe in the exam-traps segment and the stepwise-ladder probe in the management segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows both keys and reads the stem wording. Fell and recovered: updated the order after the contrast. Fell and stayed: still answers the old key; give a one-line rule for the stem wording.

traps.trap: A bedside Doppler, clinical test or venography is the investigation of choice for varicose veins (merged TR3: venography stretched to superficial reflux)

probes.stem_idea: What is the investigation of choice for varicose veins?
probes.correct: Duplex ultrasound (colour Doppler)
probes.note: hand-held Doppler = stops at screening level; venography = deep-disease gold standard stretched (TR3 variant)

probes.stem_idea: Before planning SFJ intervention you need junctional reflux, perforators and deep vein patency in one test: which test?
probes.correct: Colour duplex of the whole limb

probes.stem_idea: Which statement about investigations is NOT correct?
probes.correct: Venography is routine before varicose vein treatment
distractor_set: Hand-held Doppler detects junctional reflux but is superseded by duplex
Venography is reserved for complex deep venous disease
probes.note: all distractors are true statements; trap is the learner who treats venography/Doppler as the main test

traps.diagnoses: Learner stops at the screening level or imports the gold-standard label of deep venous disease to the superficial system.
traps.first_wrong_step: Asks 'which test sees a vein or the reflux?' instead of 'which single test shows reflux anatomy, perforators and deep patency?'.

repair.strategy: E8: ladder of tests - bedside Doppler (detects), duplex (maps), venography (deep-vein planning only)

traps.retest: vignette on planning intervention, then a which-is-NOT on the role of each test
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows duplex as the full map. Fell and recovered: placed Doppler and venography on the ladder. Fell and stayed: reaches for a familiar test name without asking what it answers.

traps.trap: The Perthes test detects SFJ incompetence and the Brodie-Trendelenburg test detects deep vein patency

probes.stem_idea: Which bedside test assesses deep vein patency?
probes.correct: Perthes test

probes.stem_idea: Tourniquet on, patient walks, calf pain and bulging veins: which test and what does it mean?
probes.correct: Perthes test; deep vein obstruction
probes.note: the maneuver (walking with tourniquet) identifies Perthes; the trap is the swapped name

probes.stem_idea: Which pairing of test and what it shows is NOT correct?
probes.correct: Perthes test - SFJ incompetence
distractor_set: Fegan's test - fascial defects at incompetent perforators

traps.diagnoses: Learner files the two tourniquet tests under one heading and swaps the names, remembering the tests but not what each one asks.
traps.first_wrong_step: Pairs a name with a function from memory of the eponym, rather than from the maneuver (compress the junction and stand vs tourniquet and walk).

repair.strategy: E10: pair recall anchored in the maneuver - what is done and what is watched - contrasted with its look-alike

traps.retest: vignette with the maneuver described, then a which-is-NOT pairing in exam traps
traps.report_hint: Avoided: reads the maneuver, not the name. Fell and recovered: now anchors each test to its maneuver. Fell and stayed: swaps eponyms; keep a maneuver-first rule.

traps.trap: On the Brodie-Trendelenburg test, filling with the tourniquet still on means SFJ incompetence

probes.stem_idea: Leg elevated, veins emptied, SFJ compressed, patient stands, veins fill rapidly while still compressed: what is incompetent?
probes.correct: Perforating veins
distractor_set: Short saphenous vein at the popliteal fossa

probes.stem_idea: Same test: no filling while compressed, rapid filling from above on release: which site and why?
probes.correct: SFJ; blood refluxes down the GSV once the compression is removed
distractor_set: Perforators; blood enters from deep to superficial under compression
Deep vein obstruction; collaterals fill the superficial system

traps.diagnoses: Learner remembers 'pressure on, watch the filling' but cannot place which filling pattern belongs to which site.
traps.first_wrong_step: Does not ask what the compression blocks: it stops reflux from the junction, so filling that still occurs must come from another entry point.

repair.strategy: E3: predict-then-show - what the compression blocks, so where blood can still enter

traps.retest: second pattern reversed (filling only on release) in a vignette
traps.report_hint: Avoided: reasons from what the compression blocks. Fell and recovered: now predicts filling route. Fell and stayed: memorises the result without the mechanism.

traps.trap: The Trendelenburg test, operation, position and sign are one thing

probes.stem_idea: Which Trendelenburg is flush ligation of the GSV at the SFJ through a groin incision?
probes.correct: Trendelenburg operation

probes.stem_idea: Clinic note: 'positive Trendelenburg' in a varicose patient versus in a patient with a limp: what does each mean?
probes.correct: Varicose: SFJ reflux test; limp: hip abductor weakness
distractor_set: Varicose: SFJ ligation done; limp: SFJ test positive
Both mean SFJ reflux on bedside testing
Varicose: hip abductor weakness; limp: SFJ reflux

traps.diagnoses: Learner treats one eponym as one concept and does not use the context words (test, operation, sign, position) to separate them.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads the eponym alone and not the noun that follows it.

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - four Trendelenburgs side by side with a one-word discriminator each

traps.retest: context-sentence vignette in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: uses the noun after the eponym. Fell and recovered: sorts the four. Fell and stayed: keep a 'name plus noun' rule.

traps.trap: The great and short saphenous veins run and terminate the same way

probes.stem_idea: Which vein runs behind the lateral malleolus and joins the popliteal vein?
probes.correct: Short (small) saphenous vein

probes.stem_idea: Match the course: GSV and SSV, malleolus and termination.
probes.correct: GSV: in front of medial malleolus to femoral vein; SSV: behind lateral malleolus to popliteal vein
distractor_set: GSV: behind lateral malleolus to popliteal vein; SSV: in front of medial malleolus to femoral vein
Both pass in front of the medial malleolus; GSV ends in the femoral vein, SSV in the popliteal vein
Both pass behind the lateral malleolus and end in the femoral vein

traps.diagnoses: Learner merges the two saphenous veins into one 'saphenous' template and loses the side (medial or lateral) and the termination.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls the shared origin at the dorsal venous arch and assumes the rest of the course is shared.

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - medial/front/femoral for the GSV vs lateral/behind/popliteal for the SSV, anchored to the dorsal arch end each starts from

traps.retest: course-and-termination contrast later in a surgical-anatomy case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates the two by arch end. Fell and recovered: anchors by medial/lateral. Fell and stayed: keep the side-to-termination rule.

traps.trap: The saphenous nerve is at risk in short saphenous surgery; the sural nerve in GSV stripping

probes.stem_idea: Nerve injured in below-knee GSV stripping?
probes.correct: Saphenous nerve

probes.stem_idea: Numbness over the lateral border of the foot after SSV surgery behind the knee: which nerve?
probes.correct: Sural nerve
distractor_set: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh

traps.diagnoses: Learner has the two nerve names and the two veins but no rule linking each nerve to the vein it accompanies.
traps.first_wrong_step: Pairs by recency or surface similarity of names, not by which vein the nerve runs beside.

repair.strategy: E10: pair recall - nerve accompanies vein (saphenous with GSV on the medial side, sural with SSV on the lateral side), contrasted with the other pair

traps.retest: vignette with the numbness territory described, in the surgery or complications segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: pairs each nerve with its vein. Fell and recovered: reasons by companion vein. Fell and stayed: the nerve pairing needs a vein-first rule.

traps.trap: The GSV is stripped all the way to the ankle

probes.stem_idea: Up to what level is the GSV stripped in the Trendelenburg operation?
probes.correct: From the groin to just below the knee
distractor_set: From the groin to the ankle
From the groin to the mid-thigh only
From the groin to the medial malleolus, with the nerve preserved

probes.stem_idea: Why is stripping stopped at the below-knee level?
probes.correct: The saphenous nerve runs with the vein below the knee
distractor_set: The sural nerve is closest to the vein in the calf
The vein is too small below the knee to strip
The deep veins join the GSV below the knee

traps.diagnoses: Learner uses a 'remove the whole vein' model and drops the qualifier tied to nerve injury.
traps.first_wrong_step: Assumes the aim is to remove all diseased vein and does not weigh what travels beside the vein below the knee.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier - to just below the knee - and tie it to the nerve that explains it

traps.retest: mechanism probe on why the extent stops where it does
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows the extent and why. Fell and recovered: ties the extent to the nerve. Fell and stayed: remembers 'strip' but not the limit.

traps.trap: Named perforators are interchangeable or placed at the wrong level

probes.stem_idea: Perforator at the medial lower leg/ankle linking the posterior arch vein to the posterior tibial veins?
probes.correct: Cockett

probes.stem_idea: Order the four named perforators from ankle upward to mid-thigh.
probes.correct: Cockett, Boyd, Dodd, Hunter

traps.diagnoses: Learner knows the four eponyms exist but has no anchor tying each name to its level on the medial leg and thigh.
traps.first_wrong_step: Retrieves the names as an unordered set and guesses the level from familiarity.

repair.strategy: E10: pair recall on a leg diagram - walk upward ankle, below knee, lower thigh, mid-thigh - and contrast with the nearest neighbour

traps.retest: ordering probe after the diagram, then use in a venous-ulcer case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: has the ankle-to-thigh walk. Fell and recovered: now orders them. Fell and stayed: names without levels.

traps.trap: Perforator valves let blood flow from deep to superficial veins

probes.stem_idea: In the normal limb, in which direction do perforator valves allow flow?
probes.correct: Superficial to deep only

probes.stem_idea: A perforator valve fails: describe what happens to the flow when the calf muscle contracts.
probes.correct: Blood is pushed back from deep into the superficial veins
distractor_set: Blood is pulled from superficial into deep veins faster
Blood stays only in the deep system
Blood drains from the superficial veins to the heart faster

traps.diagnoses: Learner carries the trunk reflux direction onto the perforators and loses the normal direction.
traps.first_wrong_step: Defines reflux by 'blood goes the wrong way' without first stating the right way for each segment.

repair.strategy: E3: predict-then-show - normal direction first (superficial to deep), then what reflux reverses

traps.retest: failed-valve vignette in the mechanism segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: states the normal direction first. Fell and recovered: now traces the flow. Fell and stayed: reasons from the disease direction only.

traps.trap: Walking raises venous pressure in the leg; the calf pump produces ambulatory venous hypertension

probes.stem_idea: What does the calf muscle pump do to venous pressure during walking in a normal leg?
probes.correct: Lowers it
distractor_set: Raises it briefly and then lowers it back

probes.stem_idea: Patient with reflux: pressure measured at the ankle fails to fall on walking. Name the state and the cause.
probes.correct: Ambulatory venous hypertension from failure of the pump to lower pressure
distractor_set: Ambulatory venous hypertension because the pump raises pressure on walking

traps.diagnoses: Learner knows symptoms worsen on standing and so reverses the pump's normal effect.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reasons from the symptom backwards to a mechanism without asking what the pump normally does.

repair.strategy: E3: trace the mechanism step by step - normal pump lowers pressure; with reflux or obstruction the fall fails

traps.retest: vignette on pressure behaviour in reflux
traps.report_hint: Avoided: starts from the normal pump. Fell and recovered: now traces the failure. Fell and stayed: reverses mechanism from symptom.

traps.trap: CEAP diameter bands and ulcer-class numbers are interchangeable (merged TR15: C4, C5, C6 order)

probes.stem_idea: In CEAP, varicose veins (C2) are defined by which diameter measured standing?
probes.correct: 3 mm or more

probes.stem_idea: Patient has a healed venous ulcer: which CEAP class?
probes.correct: C5
probes.note: C6 variant is the reversed last two classes (TR15 merged here)

traps.diagnoses: Learner remembers the numbers but not which class or vein type each belongs to.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls '1 and 3 mm' or 'C4, 5, 6' as bare numbers rather than attached to the clinical sign.

repair.strategy: E6: anchor each number to a sign - below 1 mm telangiectasia, 1 to 3 mm reticular, 3 mm or more varicose; C4 skin, C5 healed, C6 active

traps.retest: classification vignette with a clinical picture rather than a class number
traps.report_hint: Avoided: anchors number to the sign. Fell and recovered: now anchors. Fell and stayed: bare numbers; recommend sign-first recall.

traps.trap: Compression is started for a venous ulcer without measuring ABPI first

probes.stem_idea: Leg ulcer with brown pigmentation above the medial malleolus: what is the first step before starting compression?
probes.correct: Measure ABPI to exclude arterial disease

probes.stem_idea: ABPI 0.6 in a patient with a venous-looking ulcer: what do you do about compression?
probes.correct: Withhold compression and look for significant arterial disease
distractor_set: Apply compression at a lower pressure and review in a week
Apply compression and recheck ABPI after healing
Compression is safe above any ABPI

traps.diagnoses: Learner jumps to the mainstay of treatment and skips the safety check that must precede it.
traps.first_wrong_step: Fixes on compression as the answer to 'venous ulcer' and does not ask what could make compression harmful.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps - assess arterial supply, then compress - and ask what first and why

traps.retest: ABPI result vignette in the management segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: checks arterial supply first. Fell and recovered: now orders ABPI then compression. Fell and stayed: skips the safety step.

traps.trap: Compression stockings are the treatment for symptomatic varicose veins

probes.stem_idea: Fit 45-year-old with symptomatic varicose veins, suitable for intervention: what should be offered?
probes.correct: Interventional treatment (endothermal ablation)
distractor_set: Leg elevation and weight loss alone

probes.stem_idea: In which patient are graduated stockings the appropriate choice?
probes.correct: Pregnant woman with symptomatic varicose veins
distractor_set: Fit adult with GSV reflux on duplex
Adult with recurrent varicose veins and a suitable GSV
Young adult with symptomatic C2 disease, no contraindication

traps.diagnoses: Learner generalises 'compression helps symptoms' to every patient and ignores the qualifier of suitability for intervention.
traps.first_wrong_step: Retrieves 'stockings relieve symptoms' without checking whether the patient can instead have the definitive treatment.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier - stockings are for pregnancy, after treatment, or when intervention is unsuitable or declined

traps.retest: contrast probe on who gets stockings
traps.report_hint: Avoided: sorts the settings. Fell and recovered: now keys on intervention suitability. Fell and stayed: defaults to stockings.

traps.trap: Superficial vein stripping or ligation can be done without checking the deep veins

probes.stem_idea: What must be confirmed before stripping or ligation of superficial veins?
probes.correct: Deep vein patency, by Perthes test or duplex

probes.stem_idea: Perthes test: tourniquet on, walking, veins bulge with calf pain. Decision for stripping?
probes.correct: Do not strip; the superficial veins are acting as collaterals
distractor_set: Proceed with stripping; the veins have emptied
Proceed once the Brodie-Trendelenburg test is positive

probes.stem_idea: Why does deep vein occlusion contraindicate superficial surgery?
probes.correct: The superficial veins carry the collateral outflow
distractor_set: Reflux is absent when the deep system is blocked
The saphenous nerve is at risk
Anaesthesia is unsafe in deep vein disease

traps.diagnoses: Learner remembers the operation and drops the precondition; reads a positive Perthes as reassuring.
traps.first_wrong_step: Does not ask where the blood will go once the superficial veins are removed.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps and ask what first and why - confirm deep patency, then operate - with the collateral mechanism

traps.retest: decision vignette on a positive Perthes, then a mechanism probe
traps.report_hint: Avoided: checks patency first. Fell and recovered: now asks where outflow goes. Fell and stayed: operates without the precondition.

traps.trap: The most common finding is the only one (SFJ is the only site of reflux; primary is the only type)

probes.stem_idea: Most common site of reflux in varicose veins?
probes.correct: Saphenofemoral junction
probes.note: the trap is then flipped in the next probe: absolute reading of 'most common'

probes.stem_idea: Which statement about varicose vein distribution is NOT correct?
probes.correct: Reflux is seen only at the saphenofemoral junction
distractor_set: Short saphenous reflux occurs but is less common
Perforator incompetence can occur with or without trunk reflux
Secondary varicose veins follow deep vein thrombosis

traps.diagnoses: Learner reads 'most common' as 'only' and rules out the second and third options.
traps.first_wrong_step: Stores the superlative as an absolute and stops considering other sites and types.

repair.strategy: E4: show the exact qualifier and a counter-case (SSV and perforator reflux, secondary veins)

traps.retest: 'which is NOT' wording on distribution
traps.report_hint: Avoided: treats the superlative as a ranking. Fell and recovered: considers the second option. Fell and stayed: reads 'most common' as 'only'.

traps.trap: Foam sclerotherapy suits telangiectasias; liquid sclerotherapy suits large truncal veins

probes.stem_idea: Cluster of telangiectasias and reticular veins on the thigh: which sclerotherapy form suits?
probes.correct: Liquid sclerotherapy
distractor_set: Foam sclerotherapy with a larger volume

probes.stem_idea: Which statement matches sclerotherapy form to vein size?
probes.correct: Foam is more effective than liquid in larger veins
distractor_set: Liquid is more effective than foam in larger veins
Foam suits telangiectasias; liquid suits trunks
Foam and liquid have the same role at every vein size

traps.diagnoses: Learner assumes the newer foam technique applies everywhere and does not connect the form to the vein size.
traps.first_wrong_step: Treats foam as simply 'better' without asking how it works (displaces blood in a large lumen).

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier - vein size - with the Tessari foam mechanism of displacing blood

traps.retest: contrast probe on size matching
traps.report_hint: Avoided: matches the form to the vein size. Fell and recovered: now uses the mechanism. Fell and stayed: always says foam.

traps.trap: Polidocanol is wrong as the sclerosant because the classic answer is STS

probes.stem_idea: Single-best-answer: sclerosant used in sclerotherapy for varicose veins (key expects the classic agent).
probes.correct: Sodium tetradecyl sulphate
probes.note: polidocanol is withheld so the learner who holds the trap has no wrong option to pick here; the trap fires in the next probe

probes.stem_idea: Both sodium tetradecyl sulphate and polidocanol are listed: which statement about the key is correct?
probes.correct: STS is the classic key; polidocanol is an equally accepted modern agent
distractor_set: STS is correct; polidocanol is not a sclerosant
Polidocanol replaced STS and the old key is wrong
Both are wrong; the key expects ethanolamine oleate

traps.diagnoses: Learner treats the classic exam key as the only correct answer and rejects an equally valid modern option.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads 'the key says STS' as 'polidocanol is incorrect'.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - the classic key and the accepted modern agent - plus how to answer when only one is listed

traps.retest: contrast probe on key versus accepted answers
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows both are accepted. Fell and recovered: now teaches both. Fell and stayed: marks polidocanol as wrong.

traps.trap: A saphena varix and a femoral hernia share a fluid thrill and both disappear on lying down

probes.stem_idea: Groin swelling with cough impulse that vanishes on lying down and has a fluid thrill on tapping: what is it?
probes.correct: Saphena varix

probes.stem_idea: Which feature is NOT characteristic of a saphena varix?
probes.correct: Irreducible mass without a thrill
probes.note: all distractors are true features; the trap is the learner who swaps the discriminators between the two diagnoses

traps.diagnoses: Learner keeps the shared groin-swelling features (cough impulse) and loses the discriminators between saphena varix and femoral hernia.
traps.first_wrong_step: Settles on 'groin swelling with cough impulse' and stops before the discriminating features.

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - saphena varix against femoral hernia, naming the fluid thrill and emptying on lying down

traps.retest: which-is-NOT on features
traps.report_hint: Avoided: uses the discriminators. Fell and recovered: now separates the two. Fell and stayed: groin swelling reasoning only.

traps.trap: A venous ulcer sits on the toes, heel or lateral malleolus (the arterial sites)

probes.stem_idea: Most common site of a venous ulcer?
probes.correct: Gaiter area just above the medial malleolus

probes.stem_idea: A gaiter-area ulcer with pigmentation and oedema in a middle-aged woman: ulcer type and why?
probes.correct: Venous ulcer; gaiter area with skin changes of venous hypertension
distractor_set: Arterial ulcer; gaiter area is a pressure point
Neuropathic ulcer; gaiter area bears weight
Marjolin's ulcer; gaiter area is the usual site

traps.diagnoses: Learner copies the arterial 'foot ulcer' site pattern onto the venous ulcer.
traps.first_wrong_step: Locates ulcers by 'distal foot' and does not link the site to where venous pressure is highest.

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - venous at the gaiter (high pressure at the ankle) against arterial at the distal toes and heel

traps.retest: case with the ulcer described, in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: places the ulcer with the pressure. Fell and recovered: sorts venous and arterial sites. Fell and stayed: foot-ulcer default.

probe_plan: Backbone traps: TR11 and TR12 (flow direction and pump mechanism), which every later idea builds on; TR2, TR4 and TR18 (investigation ladder, the two tourniquet tests, and the deep-vein precondition), which chain into each other; TR1, TR17 and TR16 (what treatment, for whom, in what order). Planned order of first meeting: TR19 and TR7 (definition and anatomy, easy entry), then TR11, TR12 (mechanism), TR31 (ulcer site), TR2 (investigation), TR4 then TR5 and TR6 (bedside tests, with TR6 as the look-alike contrast), TR18 (precondition for surgery), TR1 then TR17 (management ladder and who gets stockings), TR9 then TR8 (stripping extent and nerves), TR16 (ABPI before compression), TR21 then TR22 (sclerotherapy form and agent), and TR10, TR14, TR24 as exam-trap closers. Shared stems: TR1 and TR17 share the management vignette; TR4, TR5 and TR18 share the Perthes and Brodie-Trendelenburg cases; TR7 and TR8, and TR9 and TR8, share an anatomy-to-complication thread; TR21 and TR22 share one sclerotherapy stem. Probes labelled with the form 'which-is-not' (TR2, TR4, TR19, TR24) belong in the exam-traps segment. Each trap is re-tested in a different form from its first probe; TR2, TR4 and TR18 get a third probe because they are highest-yield and the three most likely to be confused with each other.
